back: A building or place where goods are received, stored and protected until they are needed for production, sale or use.
The **time** gap between production and consumption (time utility).
Dividing large quantities received from producers into smaller quantities that customers can buy.
Goods are stored when supply is high and released when supply is low, evening out supply and so prices.

front: Name four functions of a warehouse besides storage.
back: Protection, breaking bulk, grading and packing, preparing goods for sale, steady supply, price stabilisation (any four).

front: Give an example of seasonal production with steady demand.
back: Maize (or cotton, groundnuts, tobacco): harvested once a year but used all year.

front: Give an example of steady production with seasonal demand.
back: School uniforms, blankets or umbrellas: made all year, bought mainly at certain times.
Indigenous granaries (Shona and Ndebele) raised off the ground to keep grain dry and away from pests.
A document showing ownership of goods in a public warehouse; it can be transferred to a buyer or used as security for a loan.
